chunks: I stood firm in the matter when they faltered, and I came forward when they hesitated, and I proceeded with the light of Allah when they stood still.
I was the quietest of them in voice but the foremost in going forward; I flew with its rein and monopolized its pledge, like the mountain which neither sweeping winds move nor storms displace.
No one had a spur (to urge me on) in me, nor any speaker had a flaw (to criticize) in me.

key_terms.فَوْتاً: Foremost or fastest in going forward
key_terms.مَغْمَزٌ: A flaw or fault for criticism

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad demonstrate leadership and steadfastness when others hesitated?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha, specifically from the sermon of 'His Steadfastness and Precedence in Islam,' highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him and his family) active leadership and clarity when others were hesitant or stagnant. It emphasizes his unique character and infallibility from any fault, using the metaphor of a mountain unshaken by storms to illustrate his resilience. The text underscores his role as the guiding light of Islam, distinguishing him from his contemporaries through his unwavering commitment and divine support.
